question: What is the primary pathological feature of degenerative joint disease?
explanation: The core disease process begins with the gradual wear and breakdown of the smooth articular cartilage covering joint surfaces. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T13#GNS222_U1_T13_h1)

question: Bone outgrowths that form at the joint margins are called what?
explanation: Mechanical stress and friction stimulate the bone to form abnormal bony projections, known as osteophytes, around the damaged joint. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T13#GNS222_U1_T13_h1)

question: The single greatest risk factor for developing degenerative joint disease is...
explanation: The lifetime accumulation of mechanical stress and reduced tissue healing capacity make age the primary risk factor. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T13#GNS222_U1_T13_h2)

question: A patient with severe knee osteoarthritis asks why excess weight matters. The best explanation is that obesity...

options.A: Reduces synovial fluid production in the joint capsule
options.B: Increases mechanical load on weight-bearing surfaces
options.C: Blocks calcium absorption in the subchondral bone
options.D: Triggers systemic antibody attacks on the synovium

explanation: Extra body mass exerts continuous physical pressure that accelerates the breakdown of cartilage in weight-bearing joints. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T13#GNS222_U1_T13_h2)

question: Morning stiffness associated with osteoarthritis typically lasts for approximately how long?
explanation: Unlike rheumatoid arthritis which features prolonged morning stiffness, osteoarthritis stiffness is brief and resolves quickly with movement. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T13#GNS222_U1_T13_h3)

question: A grating sensation felt when moving an arthritic joint is documented as...
explanation: Crepitus occurs when rough, exposed bone ends grind against each other due to the complete loss of intervening cartilage. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T13#GNS222_U1_T13_h3)

question: The primary imaging modality used to confirm osteoarthritis and visualize bone changes is...
explanation: X-rays clearly show hallmark signs such as joint space narrowing and osteophyte formation. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T13#GNS222_U1_T13_h4)

question: Why is joint aspiration performed when evaluating a patient with joint pain?

options.A: To rule out infection or systemic inflammation
options.B: To remove accumulated bone spurs from the space
options.C: To inject lubricating oil into the joint cavity
options.D: To measure the exact thickness of remaining cartilage

explanation: Synovial fluid analysis helps differentiate simple mechanical osteoarthritis from infectious or inflammatory arthropathies. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T13#GNS222_U1_T13_h4)

question: A major systemic risk associated with long-term oral nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug use is...
explanation: Inhibition of protective gastric prostaglandins by nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs puts patients at high risk for stomach ulcers and bleeding. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T13#GNS222_U1_T13_h5)

question: A patient is prescribed topical nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs for knee osteoarthritis. The nurse recognizes that this route is chosen primarily to...

options.A: Avoid the need for prescription orders

explanation: Topical delivery provides targeted pain relief at the joint while keeping drug concentration in the general bloodstream very low. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T13#GNS222_U1_T13_h5)

question: Which exercise type is most appropriate for a client with knee osteoarthritis?
explanation: Low-impact activities improve muscle support and joint mobility without subjecting cartilage to excessive jarring forces. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T13#GNS222_U1_T13_h6)

question: A client with left hip osteoarthritis is instructed to use a cane. The nurse should teach the client to hold the cane in which hand?
explanation: Holding the assistive device in the hand opposite the affected joint helps shift body weight away from the painful hip during ambulation. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T13#GNS222_U1_T13_h6)

question: The definitive surgical procedure for severe, end-stage joint degeneration is...
explanation: Total joint replacement removes damaged bone and cartilage surfaces and replaces them with artificial prosthetic components. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T13#GNS222_U1_T13_h7)

question: Following a total hip replacement surgery, a critical nursing intervention to prevent prosthesis dislocation is...

options.A: Preventing extreme hip flexion and crossing legs
options.B: Encouraging deep knee bends during physical therapy
options.C: Placing a high pillow underneath the operative knee
options.D: Massaging the surgical thigh muscles every two hours

explanation: Positioning restrictions protect the new hip joint alignment and prevent the femoral head from popping out of the socket. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T13#GNS222_U1_T13_h7)

question: What is the primary goal of nursing interventions for a client with chronic joint pain?

options.A: Promoting comfort and maintaining functional independence
options.B: Eliminating all physical activity to rest the joint
options.C: Ensuring permanent dependence on strong opioid medications
options.D: Achieving complete structural reversal of cartilage damage

explanation: Because joint degeneration is irreversible, care centers on minimizing pain while keeping the patient as active and independent as possible. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T13#GNS222_U1_T13_h8)

question: Which of the following is NOT an appropriate self-management strategy for osteoarthritis?
explanation: Complete bed rest is harmful because immobility leads to muscle atrophy, joint stiffness, and increased functional decline. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T13#GNS222_U1_T13_h8)
